description: Findings owned by this repository, swept from the docs knowledge agent's own planning documents. Every entry is self-contained: it carries its own reproduction, root cause, proposed fix, and acceptance, so a builder needs no other document.

projects.summary: Open, deferred, and never-measured items found by reading the effort's planning documents end to end, past the summary lines that call the work complete.

entries.title: ka retrieval never measured brute-force cosine search against an ANN index at full whole-docs corpus scale
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `documentation-agent` (`ka` binary), currently checked in at the agent's own tree (brute-force `vector_search`); per the ownership directory this binary's own behavior is owned by `documentation-agent`, not the plugin repo it currently sits in.

**Symptom.** No one knows whether query latency stays acceptable as the corpus grows past today's 29,538-chunk / ~tens-of-thousands-of-vectors size. The plan explicitly called for measuring this before committing to brute force, and no measurement was ever recorded.

**Reproduction.** Not reproducible as a defect — it is an unmet measurement obligation. To surface it: 1) `plan.md` §5 states "brute-force cosine is fine for thousands of chunks... Measure first — brute force may still be sub-second. If not, add an ANN index (HNSW)"; 2) `plan.md` §10 item 5 restates it as an open spike: "Vector store at scale — brute force vs. ANN. Measure in P1 before adding a dependency"; 3) grep the plan and the rust-rewrite plan for a recorded query-latency number at full corpus scale — none exists; 4) `rust/crates/retrieve/src/vector.rs` implements only brute-force `dot`/`vector_search`, no ANN path, and no benchmark harness for it was found under `rust/crates/retrieve` or `rust/crates/eval`.

**Root cause.** Not established — this is a missing measurement, not a code defect. The corpus scaled from the APM slice (thousands of chunks) to whole-docs (29,538 chunks) across P1–P2c without a corresponding latency benchmark ever being landed.

**Proposed fix.** Add a benchmark (e.g. a `cargo bench` or a timed CLI path in `rust/crates/eval`) that runs `vector_search` over the committed `corpus/embcache.bin`-derived `vectors.bin` at full scale and records p50/p95 query latency. If sub-second, close the spike with the number recorded in the plan; if not, implement the already-scoped HNSW fallback behind the existing `Retriever`/`Embedder`-style interface in `rust/crates/retrieve`.

**Acceptance.** A committed benchmark result (wall-clock ms per query) at the current corpus size, checked into `tests/` or the plan's resume section, closing open-decision item 5 with data — mirroring how Phase 9 (pipeline-parallel embed) was closed with a profiling number instead of code.

**Scope and risk.** Low risk to add a benchmark; if it reveals brute force is too slow, adding an ANN index touches `rust/crates/retrieve` (`index.rs`, `vector.rs`) and the `open`/`open_canonical` load path — a larger, gated change.

**Origin.** documentation-agent plan.

**Evidence.** Read `plan.md` §5, §10 item 5, §0. Read `rust/crates/retrieve/src/vector.rs` (brute-force only, no ANN code). No benchmark file found via search for "bench", "latency", "ANN", "HNSW" under `rust/crates/retrieve` and `rust/crates/eval`.

---

entries.title: ka whole-docs corpus LFS footprint shipped without ever confirming an LFS quota target
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `documentation-agent`, committed LFS assets at the agent's own tree{corpus/embcache.bin, model/model.safetensors, model-rerank/model.safetensors}`; owning repo per the ownership directory is `documentation-agent`.

**Symptom.** No operator sign-off record exists for an LFS budget, even though the plan required one before the first full-corpus commit, and the repo has since accumulated ~600MB+ of committed model + corpus LFS objects (measured: `model/model.safetensors` 273,474,832 bytes, `model-rerank/model.safetensors` 596,070,136 bytes, `corpus/embcache.bin` 79,335,148 bytes, `corpus/chunks.jsonl` 34,622,636 bytes).

**Reproduction.** 1) `plan.md` §6 flags LFS as the "highest-leverage change" and an "honest cost"; 2) `plan.md` §10 item 7: "LFS budget — single-corpus collapses this ~8×, but whole-docs is still bigger than APM. Confirm the LFS quota target before P1 commit."; 3) search both plan documents for "LFS quota" or "LFS budget" confirmation — the only other LFS mentions are `plan.md` line 56 ("LFS budget — needs sign-off") and narrative mentions in the rust-rewrite plan of what was shipped, never a confirmed number; 4) `du -sh` the repo's `model/`, `model-rerank/`, `corpus/` directories shows the actual committed size, with no corresponding target/ceiling documented anywhere in-repo.

**Root cause.** Not established — a missing sign-off, not a code defect.

**Proposed fix.** Record an explicit LFS quota target (or an explicit "no ceiling, size is acceptable" ruling) from the operator, and note it in the plan's resume section, closing open-decision item 7.

**Acceptance.** A single line in `plan.md` §10 or §0 recording the confirmed LFS target/ceiling, or a ruling that none is needed.

**Scope and risk.** None — documentation-only ticket, no code risk.

**Origin.** documentation-agent plan.

**Evidence.** Read `plan.md` §6, §10 item 7, line 56. Measured on-disk sizes of `model/model.safetensors`, `model-rerank/model.safetensors`, `corpus/embcache.bin`, `corpus/chunks.jsonl` under the agent's own tree.

entries.title: ka P1b structural site-region chunks may mis-rank under canonical-`us` indexing — flagged, never revisited
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `documentation-agent` resolver/index, `rust/crates/resolve/src/corpus.rs` (canonical-site build) and `rust/crates/retrieve/src/index.rs` (`open_canonical`); owning repo per the ownership directory is `documentation-agent`.

**Symptom.** A documents chunk that is structurally present only inside one site's `site-region` branch (e.g. a `gov`-only block) is embedded/indexed under the canonical `us`-resolved form. If that branch's content diverges enough from its `us` context, it can rank incorrectly for retrieval even though it is correctly filtered for display. The plan calls this out as a real, unresolved precision edge and defers action to "if eval shows misses" — but no one ever went back to check.

**Reproduction.** 1) `plan.md` §0 "P1 remaining" (c): "P1b structural-`site-region` retrieval-precision edge (a chunk wholly inside one site's branch embeds under canonical `us`; rare — note + revisit if eval shows misses)"; 2) `plan.md` §9 phase table, P1 row: "P1b structural-`site-region` edge still noted."; 3) search both plan documents and the eval question set (`tests/questions.yaml`) for a "P1b" resolution or a site-branch-specific eval case addressing this — none found; the eval's "site cases" (§8) test value-substitution correctness across sites, not this structural-embedding edge specifically.

**Root cause.** In `rust/crates/resolve`, `site-region` branches are kept as site-tagged chunks and filtered at retrieval time (per `plan.md` §6), but the chunk's *embedding* is computed once against canonical `us` context (`open_canonical`, `rust/crates/retrieve/src/index.rs`) even when the branch's real context is a non-`us` site. This is confirmed as a known, accepted (not fixed) design edge in the plan text, not something I independently diagnosed further in code.

**Proposed fix.** Add eval cases in `tests/questions.yaml` that specifically target a known `gov`-only or `us3`-only structural branch and assert the golden doc still ranks in the top-N pool for a `site=gov`/`site=us3` query (extending `ka eval -retrieval`). If misses appear, the documented fix is to key `open_canonical`'s embedding/ranking context per-branch's own site rather than always `us`.

**Acceptance.** New site-branch-specific retrieval-gate cases pass (or a documented finding that no misses exist, formally closing P1b).

**Scope and risk.** Touches only eval fixtures and, if a real miss is found, `rust/crates/retrieve/src/index.rs`'s canonical-indexing choice — a retrieval-precision change gated by the existing 85/85 offline retrieval suite as regression guard.

**Origin.** documentation-agent plan.

**Evidence.** Read `plan.md` §0, §9 (P1 row). Read `rust/crates/retrieve/src/index.rs` (`open_canonical`). Read `tests/questions.yaml` header/structure for site-case coverage.

---

entries.title: ka semantic answer cache (Phase 7.2) was never started
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `documentation-agent` (`ka` binary), `rust/crates/answer` and `rust/crates/embed`; owning repo per the ownership directory is `documentation-agent`.

**Symptom.** Every query still makes a full round trip (rerank + grounded-answer gateway calls) even for repeat/FAQ-style questions, which the rewrite plan itself identifies as "the highest-leverage reduction for real usage, since docs-question repetition is high." No caching exists.

**Reproduction.** 1) `rust-rewrite-plan.md` §Phase 7: "7.2 Semantic answer cache. Cache `query → answer (+citations)` keyed on the locally-computed candle query embedding (cosine ≥ threshold = hit)... Needs a TTL + corpus-refresh invalidation so a refresh drops stale answers."; 2) resume-pointer section: "Phase 7.2 semantic answer cache — unstarted (optional; explicitly out of scope of the Go-retirement project)."; 3) Phase 10 "Remaining" section repeats: "Phase 7.2 semantic answer cache — unstarted; explicitly out of scope of the retirement project."; 4) searched `rust/crates/answer` and `rust/crates/embed` for any cache-related type or module (`cache`, `ttl`) — none found; only `retrieve::embcache` exists, which is the corpus embedding cache, not a query→answer cache.

**Root cause.** Not applicable — unstarted feature, no code to diagnose.

**Proposed fix.** Implement a query→answer cache in a new module (e.g. `rust/crates/answer/src/cache.rs`): on each query, embed it with the existing `CandleEmbedder`, compare cosine similarity against cached query embeddings, return the cached `Answer` on a hit above threshold, and invalidate all entries on corpus refresh (hook into the existing refresh/rebuild path used by the `refresh-docs-agent` skill).

**Acceptance.** A repeated identical (or near-identical) query returns the cached answer with zero gateway calls, verified by a test that asserts no `Gateway::complete` call on a cache hit; a corpus refresh clears the cache, verified by a test that a stale-cache query re-hits the gateway after refresh.

**Scope and risk.** New, additive code path; risk is serving a stale or wrong-context answer if invalidation is imperfect — mitigate with a TTL as the plan specifies, not just refresh-triggered invalidation.

**Origin.** documentation-agent rust rewrite plan.

**Evidence.** Read `rust-rewrite-plan.md` §Phase 7 (7.2), resume-pointer section, Phase 10 "Remaining" section. Searched `rust/crates/answer/src` and `rust/crates/embed/src` for cache-related code — none found.

---

entries.title: ka full-corpus Metal GPU re-embed wall-clock timing was never captured
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `documentation-agent` (`ka` binary), `rust/crates/embed` (Metal device path) and `rust/crates/device`; owning repo per the ownership directory is `documentation-agent`.

**Symptom.** Metal GPU acceleration is wired, working, and shipped (`ka-darwin-arm64-metal` is committed and is the default pick on Apple Silicon per Phase 10/M4), but no one has ever run and recorded a full 29,538-chunk `--device metal` re-embed's wall-clock time or verified its resulting `vectors.bin` passes the 85/85 offline gate — only a 150-doc sample was measured (~2.4× vs CPU).

**Reproduction.** 1) `rust-rewrite-plan.md` document description: "full embed verified on Apple Silicon (~2.4× vs CPU, cosine 0.999953)" — a sample, not the full corpus; 2) Phase 6c: "`vectors.bin` still auto-materializes from the committed `embcache.bin` — re-embed DEFERRED as planned (query parity already proven)."; 3) "Rewrite COMPLETE" section: "Phase 8 full-corpus Metal re-embed wall-clock — Metal is wired + working; a full `--device metal` re-embed timing + byte-stability measurement was never formally captured... Optional."; 4) confirmed no `vectors.bin` exists in the repo (gitignored/regenerable per `.gitignore`), and no timing report file exists under `tests/` for a full-corpus Metal run, consistent with this never having been executed.

**Root cause.** Not applicable — an unperformed measurement, not a defect. The corpus currently in production is the original Go/Ollama-embedded set; Metal re-embed was validated only on a small sample.

**Proposed fix.** On a Metal-capable host, run `ka-darwin-arm64-metal build --semantic --device metal` (or the equivalent full-rebuild path) over the full corpus, record wall-clock time, and run the resulting vectors through `ka eval --semantic` (retrieval gate must hit 85/85) plus a cosine spot-check (`parity cross-device`) against the current CPU/Go-embedded vectors.

**Acceptance.** A recorded wall-clock number for the full-corpus Metal re-embed, and a passing 85/85 + cross-device cosine ≥0.9999 result, closing the "Optional" item explicitly.

**Scope and risk.** Low risk — this is a measurement task using already-shipped code paths (`--device metal`, `parity cross-device`); no new code required unless the measurement reveals a regression.

**Origin.** documentation-agent rust rewrite plan.

**Evidence.** Read `rust-rewrite-plan.md` Phase 6c, "Rewrite COMPLETE" remaining-items section. Confirmed absence of `vectors.bin` and any full-corpus Metal timing report under the `documentation-agent` directory tree.

---

entries.title: ka CUDA feature path has never been compiled or checked on any host
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `documentation-agent` (`ka` binary), `rust/crates/device` (`DevicePref::Cuda` arm) and the `cuda` Cargo feature threaded through `rust/crates/cli`, `rust/crates/embed`, `rust/crates/rerank`.

**Symptom.** The `cuda` feature and `DevicePref::Cuda` code path exist in source but have never once been built or type-checked, because no NVIDIA host is available. `cargo check --features cuda` has literally never run.

**Reproduction.** 1) `rust-rewrite-plan.md` Phase 8, task 6: "`cargo check --features cuda` deferred to a CUDA host."; 2) Phase 10 "Remaining" section: "CUDA `cargo check --features cuda` — host-gated (no NVIDIA host); compile-gated code only."; 3) confirmed `cuda` appears in `rust/crates/device/Cargo.toml`, `rust/crates/cli/Cargo.toml`, `rust/crates/embed/Cargo.toml`, `rust/crates/rerank/Cargo.toml` as a feature name, consistent with it being wired but never exercised; 4) this workstation has no CUDA toolchain (no `nvcc`/`nvidia-smi` expected), so the check cannot be run here either — consistent with the plan's own statement.

**Root cause.** Not established — the code has literally never been compiled under the `cuda` feature, so whether it even builds is unknown; this is a known-unknown, not a diagnosed bug.

**Proposed fix.** On any CUDA-capable Linux host, run `cargo check --features cuda -p ka` (or the equivalent per-crate check) inside `rust/`, fix any compile errors surfaced, and record the result. Do not claim CUDA support works until this has run at least once.

**Acceptance.** A clean `cargo check --features cuda` (and ideally `cargo build --features cuda`) result recorded from a real CUDA host, or a documented compile failure with a follow-up ticket if it fails.

**Scope and risk.** No risk to the shipped baseline — the `cuda` feature is off by default in every shipped build; this only affects whether the compile-gated code is even valid Rust.

**Origin.** documentation-agent rust rewrite plan.

**Evidence.** Read `rust-rewrite-plan.md` Phase 8 task 6, Phase 10 "Remaining" section. Confirmed `cuda` feature references in `rust/crates/device/Cargo.toml`, `rust/crates/cli/Cargo.toml`, `rust/crates/embed/Cargo.toml`, `rust/crates/rerank/Cargo.toml`.

---

entries.title: ka's four non-darwin-arm64 shipped binaries have never been executed on their native platforms
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `documentation-agent`, committed binaries `.bin/ka-linux-amd64`, `.bin/ka-linux-arm64`, `.bin/ka-darwin-amd64` (all confirmed present on disk); `.bin/ka-darwin-arm64` and `.bin/ka-darwin-arm64-metal` are the only ones built and run on the actual build host (Apple Silicon).

**Symptom.** Four of the five distributed platform binaries have only ever been cross-compiled (via `cargo-zigbuild`) and never actually executed — there is no confirmation that `ka-linux-amd64`, `ka-linux-arm64`, and `ka-darwin-amd64` even start, let alone pass the eval gate, on their target platforms.

**Reproduction.** 1) `rust-rewrite-plan.md` Phase 10 "Remaining" section: "Cross-platform binary execution — the 4 non-darwin-arm64 binaries are committed LFS objects, not yet executed on their native hosts (deferred per this plan)."; 2) the "De-risk run" section shows only a build+`ka version` check on darwin-arm64, and the empirical eval runs (85/85, 98/98) were run on "this host" (Apple Silicon), never confirmed cross-platform; 3) confirmed on disk: `.bin/ka-linux-amd64`, `.bin/ka-linux-arm64`, `.bin/ka-darwin-amd64`, `.bin/ka-darwin-arm64`, `.bin/ka-darwin-arm64-metal` all present as committed files in the repo, consistent with "built and shipped, not run."

**Root cause.** Not established — untested cross-compiled artifacts, not a diagnosed defect. Risk is speculative until run: static-musl Linux builds are generally reliable from a clean cross-compile, but self-location (`exe_dir()`), model-asset path resolution, and the semantic-default fallback logic have only been exercised on darwin-arm64 in practice.

**Proposed fix.** On a Linux x86_64 host, a Linux ARM64 host, and an Intel Mac (or equivalent), run each binary's `version` and `query --json` (or `eval --semantic`) subcommands against the committed corpus/model assets and confirm they behave identically to the darwin-arm64 baseline, including the `exe_dir()` self-location fix (Phase 10 bonus fix) and the semantic-default → BM25-fallback path when Metal/CUDA is unavailable.

**Acceptance.** A recorded pass for `<binary> version` and `<binary> eval --semantic` (85/85 minimum) on each of the three untested platforms.

**Scope and risk.** No code risk from running the test; if it fails, the fix would land in `rust/crates/cli` (self-location) or `rust/crates/device` (fallback logic), gated by the existing eval suite.

**Origin.** documentation-agent rust rewrite plan.

**Evidence.** Read `rust-rewrite-plan.md` Phase 10 "Remaining" section and the "De-risk run" section. Confirmed presence of all five `.bin/ka-*` files under the agent's own tree.

---

entries.title: ka's binary and build tooling still physically live in the the repository that ships the agent plugin repo, not in the owning documentation-agent repo
entries.feedback:
**Component.** All of `documentation-agent`'s Rust code, binaries, corpus, and models — currently at the agent's own tree{rust/, .bin/, corpus/, model/, model-rerank/}`. Per the fleet ownership directory (`workspace/.dat/root-repo-realignment/ownership-directory.md`), `documentation-agent` is listed as the CLI repo owning "the documentation knowledge agent" binary, and the ownership rule states "A plugin that provisions a binary is not that binary's owner. The two split."

**Symptom.** The `documentation-agent` repo exists but is empty of any `ka`-related code — it contains only a generic `README.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`mise.toml` scaffold with no reference to the docs knowledge agent. Meanwhile the entire binary, its Rust source, its corpus, and its ~940MB of committed model/corpus LFS assets sit inside the `the repository that ships the agent` plugin repo (which per the same directory should own only the plugin's skills/agents/hooks, not the binary).

**Reproduction.** 1) Read the ownership directory: `documentation-agent — the documentation knowledge agent` is listed under "CLI repos, each owning its own binary"; the rule states plugin and binary "split."; 2) `ls a local path shows only `CLAUDE.md`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `git-tools.yaml`, `mise.lock`, `mise.toml`, `navigator.toml` — no Rust code, no `ka` binary, no corpus; 3) `ls .../the agent's own tree shows `rust/`, `.bin/`, `corpus/`, `model/`, `model-rerank/`, `plan.md`, `rust-rewrite-plan.md` — the full binary's engine and assets, still inside the plugin repo.

**Root cause.** The plan documents were written and executed entirely under the assumption of a single combined plugin+binary repo (this predates the root-repo-realignment split); no migration step to `documentation-agent` has been performed for this component.

**Proposed fix.** Move `rust/`, `.bin/`, `corpus/`, `model/`, `model-rerank/`, `taxonomy.json`, `regions.json`, `unsupported.json`, `build.sh` from the agent's own tree into `documentation-agent`, preserving LFS history where feasible; leave the agent's own tree and the agent's own tree in `the repository that ships the agent`, updated to invoke the binary from its new location (mirroring how the `git-tools`/`workspace-tools` splits were done elsewhere in this fleet).

**Acceptance.** `documentation-agent` contains the `ka` binary/source/corpus/models and builds/evals green from there; `the repository that ships the agent`'s agent `.md` and refresh skill successfully shell out to the relocated binary; no `ka`-specific code remains under the agent's own tree except the thin agent-face wiring.

**Scope and risk.** Large, mechanical move touching two repos' git history and CI/build paths (`rust/build.sh` output naming, `refresh-docs-agent` skill's shell-out paths, the agent `.md`'s `$KA` resolver). High blast radius for a repo-history operation — coordinate with whatever other root-repo-realignment work is already in flight to avoid a duplicate move.

**Origin.** Fleet ownership directory, cross-referenced against the documentation-agent plan and rust rewrite plan.

**Evidence.** Read `workspace/.dat/root-repo-realignment/ownership-directory.md`. Listed contents of a local path and a local path.
